Coding.description: Used for DSA/coding questions. Evaluate the candidate's verbal or written approach, not just whether code compiles.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Does the proposed approach actually solve the problem, including on non-trivial inputs?

criteria.name: Approach & Algorithm Choice
criteria.description: Is the chosen technique appropriate for the problem (matches the canonical pattern retrieved), or is it a worse-than-necessary approach the candidate didn't recognize?

criteria.name: Time & Space Complexity
criteria.description: Can the candidate state and justify the complexity of their approach, and identify if a better bound exists?

criteria.name: Edge Case Handling
criteria.description: Does the candidate proactively address edge cases (empty input, single element, duplicates, etc.) relevant to this problem?

criteria.name: Communication & Code Quality
criteria.description: Is the explanation clear and structured? If code was written, is it readable and reasonably organized?

Theory.description: Used for conceptual/theory questions (OS, DBMS, networking, language fundamentals, ML theory, etc.).

criteria.name: Conceptual Correctness
criteria.description: Is the core explanation factually correct against the canonical explanation retrieved for this topic?

criteria.name: Depth & Completeness
criteria.description: Does the answer cover the key points expected for this concept, not just a surface-level definition?

criteria.name: Clarity of Communication
criteria.description: Is the explanation structured and understandable, appropriate for explaining to a colleague?

criteria.name: Real-World Grounding
criteria.description: Does the candidate connect the concept to a concrete example or practical implication, rather than reciting a definition?

Design.description: Used for System Design and LLD questions.

criteria.name: Requirements Clarification
criteria.description: Did the candidate clarify scope/constraints before designing, rather than assuming requirements?

criteria.name: Architecture & Component Design
criteria.description: Are the major components/classes identified with clear responsibilities, matching sound design principles for this problem type?

criteria.name: Tradeoff Reasoning
criteria.description: Does the candidate explicitly justify design choices (e.g., consistency vs availability, SQL vs NoSQL, caching strategy) rather than asserting them?

criteria.name: Edge Cases & Failure Handling
criteria.description: Does the design address failure modes, concurrency, or scale limits relevant to the problem?

criteria.name: Communication
criteria.description: Is the design walked through in a structured, logical order?

Behavioral.description: Used for behavioral questions. Grounded against the STAR method canonical explanation.

criteria.name: Situation & Task Clarity
criteria.description: Is the context concise and sufficient to understand the stakes, without over-explaining?

criteria.name: Action Specificity
criteria.description: Does the candidate describe what THEY specifically did, in first person, rather than what the team did in general?

criteria.name: Result & Impact
criteria.description: Is there a concrete, ideally quantified outcome, rather than a vague 'it worked out' statement?

criteria.name: Reflection
criteria.description: Does the candidate show learning or self-awareness about the experience?

criteria.name: Communication
criteria.description: Is the answer well-structured and appropriately concise?
